Based on the data you provided, the short answer is: **Yes, you would almost certainly be able to see it.**

Here is the breakdown of why the Moon will be visible to you in those specific conditions:

### 1. Altitude and Horizon
The Moon’s altitude is **5.272 degrees**. While this is relatively low in the sky (about the height of a large building or a few trees above the horizon), it is well above the "geometric" horizon. In a clear sky, anything above 5 degrees is generally easy to spot, provided there are no immediate physical obstructions (like a tall hill or a large building) directly in your line of sight.

### 2. Azimuth (Direction)
The azimuth is **59.687 degrees**. Since 0 degrees is North and 90 degrees is East, the Moon is currently in the **East-North-East** part of the sky. Because it is so low and in that direction, you would need to look toward the eastern horizon.

### 3. Illumination and Brightness
The Moon is **88.2% illuminated**. This means it is a Waxing Gibbous moon, very close to being a Full Moon. Because it is so highly illuminated, it will be very bright. It won't be a faint object; it will be a prominent, glowing presence in the sky.

### 4. Sky Conditions (Nautical Twilight)
You mentioned the sky is in **nautical twilight** and **clear**. 
*   **Nautical Twilight:** This is the period when the horizon is still visible, but the sky is dark enough for navigation by the stars. This is the perfect time to see a bright moon; the sky is dark enough to provide contrast, but it isn't "pitch black" yet.
*   **Clear Skies:** Without cloud cover to diffuse or block the light, a moon at 88% illumination will be very striking.

### The Verdict
Because the Moon is nearly full and the sky is clear, it will be one of the brightest objects in the sky. Even at a low altitude of 5 degrees, it will be quite obvious. 

**If you are trying to avoid seeing it:** You should look away from the East-North-East horizon. If there are trees or buildings in that direction, they will likely block it from your view. If you have a completely unobstructed view of the eastern horizon, it will be very difficult to miss.
